mainTopic: Days next to the holidays of מגילת תענית: why some days are listed twice, and how רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן rule
overview: מגילת תענית is a list of happy days on which fasting and eulogies are forbidden. The גמרא explains that a day which is already a holiday, like פסח or ראש חודש ניסן, is listed only to forbid the day next to it. This follows רבי יוסי, who forbids both the day before and the day after. The גמרא then challenges this. The 29th of אדר is already forbidden because it comes after the 28th, the day Rome's decree against Torah, ברית מילה and שבת was cancelled. אביי answers that the listing matters when אדר has 30 days. רב אשי answers that the 29th, sitting between two holidays, forbids even הספד. The גמרא adds a third answer: a second listing keeps a day forbidden even if the first celebration is cancelled, which also explains why the שבועות line starts from the eighth of ניסן. Finally, רב rules like רבי יוסי, and שמואל first rules like רבי מאיר and then switches to the more lenient רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי יוחנן is reported to rule like רבי יוסי for the no-fasting days, and the גמרא begins challenging that report from an unnamed משנה about reading the מגילה early, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A listed holiday is there to forbid the day next to it
steps.stepSummary: Just as ראש חודש ניסן was listed only to forbid the day before it, פסח is listed only to forbid the day after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was listed only to forbid the day before it. Here too, it was needed only to forbid the day after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer it began just before this. It explains why מגילת תענית mentions פסח even though mourning on פסח is already forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing a day that is already a holiday seems pointless. The answer is that the listing is not about the day itself but about the day next to it. Earlier, ראש חודש ניסן was explained as forbidding the day before it, and in the same way פסח forbids the day after it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (a phrase that explains why something that seems extra was written)
To forbid
The day before it
The day after it

phrases.english: only to forbid the day before it,
phrases.notes: "It" is ראש חודש ניסן, listed only so the day before it is forbidden.

phrases.english: here too, it was needed
only to forbid the day after it.
phrases.notes: "Here" means פסח, which is listed so that the day after it is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי לָא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לֶאֱסוֹר יוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a listing which seems extra has a purpose for the next day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing פסח in מגילת תענית adds nothing, since mourning on פסח is already forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing is there to forbid the day after פסח.

steps.title: This follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this is and answers: רבי יוסי, who forbids both the day before and the day after.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom is this? According to רבי יוסי, who said: it is forbidden both on the day before and on the day after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא behind the previous answer. Only רבי יוסי holds that both the day before and the day after a listed day are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer works only if the days next to a listed day are also forbidden, both before it and after it. The גמרא ties this to רבי יוסי. This sets up the next question, which uses רבי יוסי's own rule to challenge the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (asking which sage holds this view)
The תנא who forbids both the day before and the day after
Both before it and after it

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Yosei, who said:
both before it and after it, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the sage whose view the previous answer follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the days next to a listed day are forbidden?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי, who forbids both the day before and the day after.

steps.title: The 29th of אדר is already forbidden for another reason
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי forbids the day after a listed day, then the 29th of אדר is already forbidden because it comes after the 28th. So why list ראש חודש ניסן to forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then for the twenty-ninth as well, why say it is forbidden specifically because it is the day before the day the תמיד was established? Let it be forbidden because it is the day after the twenty-eighth of the month!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יוסי's own rule to attack the earlier answer about ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ראש חודש ניסן (the day the תמיד was established) was said to be listed only to forbid the 29th of אדר, the day before it. But the 28th of אדר is also a listed happy day. Under רבי יוסי, the day after it, the 29th, is already forbidden, so listing ראש חודש ניסן seems unnecessary again.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem that follows from what was just said)
Why specifically this reason?
Let him get it from a different reason
The daily offering (תמיד)

phrases.english: If so, regarding the twenty-ninth as well —
phrases.notes: The twenty-ninth of אדר, the last day before ראש חודש ניסן.

phrases.english: why specifically because it is the day
before the day on which the daily offering was established?
phrases.notes: That day is ראש חודש ניסן.

phrases.english: Let him derive it from the fact that it is
the day after the twenty-eighth of the month!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה נָמֵי מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יוסי's rule, just identified, and turns it against the earlier answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ראש חודש ניסן is listed only to forbid the 29th of אדר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוסי the 29th is already forbidden as the day after the 28th, so the listing of ראש חודש ניסן is still unexplained.

steps.title: The 28th of אדר is a listed happy day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from מגילת תענית shows that the 28th of אדר is a day of celebration: good news came that Jews would not be kept from Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: on the twenty-eighth of the month, good news came to the Jews that they would not be kept away from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that the 28th of אדר is really a happy day, which is what the challenge depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the 28th of אדר is itself a listed day. This ברייתא confirms that it is: it marks good news about being allowed to learn Torah again.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Good news
They would not be removed or kept away
The Torah

phrases.english: As it is taught: On the twenty-eighth of it,
good news came to the Jews
that they would not be kept away from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim inside the challenge that the 28th of אדר is a listed day.
steps.raayaObject: That the 28th of אדר is a day of celebration in מגילת תענית.

steps.title: Rome's decree and the plan of יהודה בן שמוע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells how Rome banned Torah study, ברית מילה and keeping שבת, and how יהודה בן שמוע and his friends went for advice to an influential Roman noblewoman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the wicked kingdom issued a decree of forced conversion against the Jews: that they not study Torah, that they not circumcise their sons, and that they break שבת. What did יהודה בן שמוע and his friends do? They went and took advice from a certain noblewoman whom all the great men of Rome used to visit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the background story of the 28th of אדר, describing the decree and the first step the leaders took.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree attacked three basic parts of Jewish life: Torah, ברית מילה and שבת. The Jewish leaders did not act on their own; they went to a woman with close ties to Rome's powerful men.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked kingdom (Rome)
A decree forcing Jews to give up their religion
The leader who led the response
A Roman noblewoman

phrases.english: For once the wicked kingdom decreed

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יַעַסְקוּ בַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: a decree of forced conversion on Israel, that they not study Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא יָמוּלוּ אֶת בְּנֵיהֶם, וְשֶׁיְּחַלְּלוּ שַׁבָּתוֹת.
phrases.english: and that they not circumcise their sons, and that they break Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה יְהוּדָה בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ וַחֲבֵרָיו?
phrases.english: What did Yehuda ben Shammua and his colleagues do?
They went and took advice from a certain noblewoman
whom all the great men of Rome used to visit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the background of the 28th of אדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rome banned Torah, ברית מילה and שבת, and the Jewish leaders went to a well-connected noblewoman for advice.

steps.title: Crying out at night, and the decree is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: Following the noblewoman's advice, the Jews protested at night. The decrees were cancelled, and that day was made a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: She told them: go and cry out at night. They went and cried out at night, saying: Heavens! Are we not brothers? Are we not children of one father? Are we not children of one mother? How are we different from every other nation and language, that you make cruel decrees against us? And they cancelled the decrees, and that day was made a יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: the night protest worked, the decree was cancelled, and the day became a celebration. This proves the 28th of אדר is a listed happy day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The protesters appealed to the Romans' sense of fairness: we are all one family, so why single us out? The cancellation of the decree is the reason the 28th of אדר was made a יום טוב. That gives the challenge in step 3 its force.

keyTerms.meaning: Cry out in public protest
O Heavens!
Cruel decrees
A day of celebration

steps.whatToRemember: The 28th of אדר is a happy day in מגילת תענית. Under רבי יוסי, that would already forbid the 29th, which is why the earlier answer about ראש חודש ניסן is in trouble.

phrases.english: She said to them: Arise and cry out at night.

phrases.aramaic: הָלְכוּ וְהִפְגִּינוּ בַּלַּיְלָה, אָמְרוּ: אֵי שָׁמַיִם!
phrases.english: They went and cried out at night, saying: O Heaven!

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אַחִים אֲנַחְנוּ, לֹא בְּנֵי אָב אֶחָד אֲנַחְנוּ,
phrases.english: Are we not brothers? Are we not children of one father?
Are we not children of one mother?
How are we different from every nation and language
that you issue cruel decrees against us!

phrases.aramaic: וּבִטְּלוּם, וְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם עֲשָׂאוּהוּ יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: And they cancelled them, and that day they made into a holiday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 5 and shows how the day became a celebration.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the decree was cancelled, the 28th of אדר was made a יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי: listing ראש חודש ניסן matters when אדר has 30 days
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the listing of ראש חודש ניסן is needed for a year when אדר has 30 days. Then the day before ראש חודש is the 30th, which does not come right after the 28th.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it was needed only for a full, 30-day month.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from step 3 and saves the idea that ראש חודש ניסן is listed to forbid the day before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אדר has only 29 days, the day before ראש חודש is the 29th, which is already forbidden as the day after the 28th. When אדר has 30 days, the day before ראש חודש is the 30th, which is two days after the 28th, so it is not covered. Only the listing of ראש חודש ניסן forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer
A "full" month of 30 days

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוסי, listing ראש חודש ניסן is needed only for a 30-day אדר, where it forbids the 30th of אדר.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חודש מעובר does not mean a leap year with an extra month of אדר. It means that אדר itself has 30 days instead of 29.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rescues the rule that a listed holiday also forbids the day next to it. It shows that a listing which seems extra can still have a real use in some years.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It was needed
only for a full month.
phrases.notes: A month of 30 days, so the day before ראש חודש is the 30th, not the 29th.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְחֹדֶשׁ מְעוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 3, now that the ברייתא has shown the 28th of אדר is a happy day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule to a specific case: a 30-day אדר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing ראש חודש ניסן is pointless, because the day before it is always already forbidden as the day after the 28th.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a 30-day אדר, the day before ראש חודש is the 30th. Only the listing of ראש חודש ניסן forbids that day.

steps.title: רב אשי: The 29th is stricter because it sits between two holidays
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even in a 29-day אדר, listing ראש חודש ניסן is needed. The day after a listed day forbids only fasting, but the 29th lies between two holidays, so it was made a full holiday where even הספד is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say the month has only 29 days, there is still a reason to list ראש חודש ניסן. Normally, a day that comes after a listed holiday forbids fasting but allows eulogies. But the 29th of אדר sits between two holidays, the 28th and ראש חודש ניסן. So the Sages made it like a holiday itself, and even eulogies are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the question from step 3. Even in a short month, listing ראש חודש ניסן adds something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי answered the question only for a 30-day אדר. רב אשי answers it even for a 29-day אדר. The day after the 28th would only forbid fasting, but because the 29th is squeezed between two holidays, it becomes stricter and also forbids הספד.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'short' month of 29 days
A fast day
A eulogy for someone who died
Placed between two holidays

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the day after a holiday is always as strict as the holiday itself. Usually it forbids only fasting. The 29th is stricter only because it sits between two holidays.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say it is a short (29-day) month,
phrases.notes: He means a year when אדר has 29 days, so the 29th comes right after the 28th and right before ראש חודש.

phrases.english: all days that come after a listed day,
fasting is forbidden, but eulogizing is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה, הוֹאִיל וּמוּטָל בֵּין שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים
phrases.english: But this day, since it lies between two holidays,
they made it like a holiday itself,
and even eulogizing is forbidden too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְחוֹדֶשׁ חָסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, next to אביי's, to the question in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes levels of strictness: the day after a holiday forbids only fasting, while a day between two holidays forbids הספד too.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing ראש חודש ניסן adds nothing in a 29-day אדר, since the 29th is already forbidden as the day after the 28th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing makes the 29th a full holiday where even הספד is forbidden, which the day-after rule alone would not do.

steps.title: Quoting the line about the eighth of ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes מגילת תענית: from the eighth of ניסן until the end of פסח, the festival of שבועות was restored, and eulogizing is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: From the eighth of ניסן until the end of the festival of פסח, the festival of שבועות was restored, and so one may not eulogize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from מגילת תענית. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line forbids הספד from the eighth of ניסן through the end of פסח. The גמרא will ask why the line starts at the eighth rather than the ninth.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said': the opening words when the גמרא quotes an earlier text again
The festival (here, פסח)
Was restored, was set back in place
The festival of שבועות

phrases.english: The Master said:
From the eighth of it until the end of the festival,
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means of the month of ניסן.

phrases.english: the festival of שבועות was restored,
so as not to eulogize.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִתְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ וְעַד סוֹף מוֹעֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a new line of מגילת תענית that raises a similar question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the eighth of ניסן until the end of פסח, הספד is forbidden because שבועות was restored.

steps.title: Why start from the eighth if it is already forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The eighth of ניסן is already forbidden as one of the days of the תמיד celebration. So why doesn't the line simply start from the ninth?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to say 'from the eighth'? Let it say 'from the ninth,' and the eighth itself is already forbidden, because it is a day on which the daily offering was set up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording 'from the eighth.' The eighth is already covered by an earlier listing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier line of מגילת תענית already forbids the days up to the eighth because of the תמיד. Listing the eighth again for שבועות seems to repeat it for no reason. This is the same kind of question as the one about ראש חודש ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks why words are written that seem unneeded)
Itself
The daily offering (תמיד)

phrases.english: Why do I need it to say 'from the eighth of it'?
Let it say 'from the ninth of it,'
and the eighth itself is forbidden anyway,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹמָא דְּאִיתּוֹקַם בֵּיהּ תְּמִידָא!
phrases.english: since it is a day on which the daily offering was set up!
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier line: from ראש חודש ניסן until the eighth, the daily offering was set up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the line quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'from the eighth' in the שבועות line of מגילת תענית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The eighth is already forbidden by the תמיד listing, so including it again seems to repeat it.

steps.title: The eighth stands on its own if the earlier days are canceled
steps.stepSummary: If some event caused the תמיד celebration days to be canceled, the eighth would still be forbidden, because it is the first day of the שבועות celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since if something happened and they canceled the seven days, the eighth itself would still be forbidden, because it is the first day on which the festival of שבועות was restored.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the eighth needs its own listing. That way it stays forbidden even if the earlier celebration is canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two listings are not just repeats. Each one is a separate reason. If the תמיד days were ever canceled, the שבועות listing would still keep the eighth forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Something happened (an event that comes up)
They canceled it
The first day

phrases.english: Since if something happened
and they canceled the seven days,
the eighth itself would still be forbidden,
since it is the first day
on which the festival of שבועות was restored.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִקְּלַע לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא וּבַטְּלִינֵּיהּ לְשִׁבְעָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Independent backup reason: the second listing protects the day in case the first is canceled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing the eighth again is a needless repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eighth needs its own reason so it stays forbidden even if the תמיד days are canceled.

steps.title: The same logic gives a third answer for the 29th of אדר
steps.stepSummary: Using the same idea, the גמרא explains listing ראש חודש ניסן: if the 28th of אדר were canceled, the 29th would still be forbidden as the day before ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this idea, the same works for the 29th too: if something happened and they canceled the 28th, the 29th itself would still be forbidden, because it is the day before the day on which the daily offering was set up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the backup-reason idea and uses it to answer the original question about ראש חודש ניסן another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 29th of אדר is forbidden for two separate reasons. It is the day after the 28th, and it is the day before ראש חודש ניסן. Listing ראש חודש ניסן keeps the 29th forbidden even if the 28th's celebration is ever canceled.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this idea
Which is before

steps.whatToRemember: A day can be forbidden for more than one reason. מגילת תענית lists the second reason so the day stays forbidden even if the first reason is canceled. This explains both 'from the eighth' of ניסן and the listing of ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a third answer to the question from step 3, next to אביי's and רב אשי's answers.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this idea,
the twenty-ninth also works the same way:
since if something happened
and they canceled the twenty-eighth,
the twenty-ninth itself would still be forbidden,
since it is the day before
the day on which the daily offering was set up.
phrases.notes: That day is ראש חודש ניסן, when the celebration for the daily offering begins.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, עֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the logic of step 11 and uses it on the question from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Independent backup reason, applied by comparison to the case of the eighth of ניסן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing ראש חודש ניסן adds nothing for the 29th, which is already forbidden as the day after the 28th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing keeps the 29th forbidden as the day before ראש חודש ניסן, even if the 28th's celebration is canceled.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about whose opinion is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי יוסי (the days before and after a listed day are also forbidden). שמואל rules like רבי מאיר (the day before is forbidden, the day after is permitted).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב חייא בר אסי said in the name of רב, 'The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.' שמואל said, 'The הלכה follows רבי מאיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement between two אמוראים about which תנא from the משנה we follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says that for a no-eulogy day, the day before is forbidden but the day after is permitted. רבי יוסי forbids both the day before and the day after. רב picks the stricter view, and שמואל picks the more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an argument between אמוראים)
The final ruling follows...

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Asi said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי is the one in the משנה who forbids both the day before and the day after.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר is the unnamed opinion in the משנה, who permits the day after.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the dates in מגילת תענית to the practical ruling on the days around them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: הלכה like רבי יוסי. שמואל: הלכה like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: שמואל elsewhere rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל could rule like רבי מאיר, when he also ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who permits both the day before and the day after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? A ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Why does it say 'on them' twice? To teach that only the days themselves are forbidden, while the days before and after are permitted. And שמואל said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with another ruling of his that seems to contradict this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from the double word 'בהון' that only the listed days themselves are forbidden. If שמואל rules like him, the day before is permitted too. That cannot match ruling like רבי מאיר, who forbids the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a contradiction)
But a ברייתא teaches...
On them (a word in מגילת תענית)
Why does the text say...

phrases.english: But did Shmuel really say this?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
What does it teach by saying "on them," "on them" twice?
phrases.notes: In מגילת תענית: 'not to eulogize on them' and 'not to fast on them.'

phrases.english: To tell you that they themselves are forbidden,
but the days before them and after them are permitted.
And Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל cannot rule like two different opinions. רבי מאיר forbids the day before, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permits it.

steps.title: שמואל changed his mind to the most lenient opinion
steps.stepSummary: At first שמואל thought רבי מאיר was the most lenient, so he ruled like him. When he heard that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was even more lenient, he switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he thought no תנא was as lenient as רבי מאיר, so he ruled like רבי מאיר. Once he heard that רבן שמעון was even more lenient, he ruled like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two rulings come from different times: שמואל changed his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's real goal was always to follow the most lenient opinion on this topic. So the two rulings do not contradict each other. The second one replaced the first after he learned of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: At first he held...
Is lenient
More

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל consistently followed the most lenient view here. His later ruling, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, replaced his earlier one.

phrases.english: At first he held:
since there is no tanna
who is as lenient as Rabbi Meir,
he said the halacha follows Rabbi Meir.
Once he heard that Rabban Shimon
is even more lenient,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: he said: The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of mind over time (earlier and later ruling)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two rulings clash, as if he held two opinions at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל first ruled like רבי מאיר and later switched to the more lenient רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: באלי reports in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, the same as רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, באלי said that רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא, רבי יוחנן, who rules the same way as רב. This sets up the clarification in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' shows that this ruling backs up רב's position from step 13. The next step will narrow how far this ruling goes.

keyTerms.meaning: And so too (agreeing with an earlier view)
A sage who passes on this teaching

phrases.english: And so too Bali said
that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's side of the argument from step 13 and adds רבי יוחנן's agreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling covers only the no-fasting days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains to באלי that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי only about the days marked 'not to fast.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to באלי: Let me explain it to you. When רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, he meant only about the days of 'not to fast.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבי יוחנן's ruling. It applies only to the no-fasting days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has separate rules for no-eulogy days and no-fasting days, and רבי יוסי has an opinion on each. רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי only for the no-fasting days. He does not follow him for the no-eulogy days, so he is not fully on רב's side.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me explain it to you
'Not to fast' (the label for no-fasting days in מגילת תענית)
'Not to eulogize' (the label for no-eulogy days in מגילת תענית)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יוחנן agrees with רב on everything. His ruling like רבי יוסי covers only the no-fasting days, not the no-eulogy days.
steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבי יוסי. שמואל ends up with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי only for the no-fasting days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said to Bali:
Let me explain it to you:
When Rabbi Yochanan said
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,
it was about "not to fast."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the ruling from step 16 reaches.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי only for the no-fasting days in מגילת תענית.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really rule like רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי. רבי יוחנן also taught that the law follows an unnamed משנה, and the גמרא begins quoting an unnamed משנה about reading the מגילה early.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But didn't רבי יוחנן say that the law follows an unnamed משנה? And we learned in a משנה: Even though the Sages said that one may read the מגילה earlier but not later...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning whether רבי יוחנן could really have ruled like רבי יוסי. It starts quoting a משנה that it will use against him, and the quote finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general rule: when a משנה states a law with no name attached, that is the final law. So if an unnamed משנה disagrees with רבי יוסי, רבי יוחנן should follow the משנה and not רבי יוסי. This step sets up that clash by bringing in the משנה about reading the מגילה early.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say this? This is how the גמרא opens a challenge to a reported ruling.
But didn't he say...? This brings in a different statement by the same person that seems to clash.
An unnamed משנה, a law stated without naming which Sage said it.
And we learned, in a משנה.
One may do it earlier, but not later.

steps.confusionAlert: The quote from the משנה is not finished here. The part that actually causes the problem comes on the next amud, so don't try to find the contradiction in these words alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'the law follows an unnamed משנה' is one of רבי יוחנן's major rules for deciding הלכה. The גמרא uses it here to test whether the report of his ruling holds up.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
The law follows an unnamed mishna.
And we learned: Even though they said
that one may do it earlier but not later,
phrases.notes: This comes from the משנה in מגילה, about reading the מגילה before פורים in some places, never after.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the ruling reported in steps 16 and 17, that רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי, by using another rule of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי about the days marked 'not to fast'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds that the law follows an unnamed משנה. The unnamed משנה in מגילה, which starts being quoted here, will turn out to disagree with רבי יוסי, so רבי יוחנן should not rule like רבי יוסי.
